$comment: Publish options for azure.synapse.tools, per environment.
Read by scripts/Deploy-Synapse.ps1 and translated into the module's own
New-SynapsePublishOption object.
IMPORTANT - what this tool does and does NOT deploy:
DOES deploy   workspace artifacts - linked services, datasets, notebooks,
SQL script tabs, Synapse pipelines, triggers, Spark job
definitions. These live in the workspace's own artifact store
and are reached through the Dev API (<ws>.dev.azuresynapse.net).
Does NOT deploy   anything INSIDE the serverless SQL database. Databases,
schemas, external data sources, file formats, views and
procedures are ordinary T-SQL objects. No artifact API can
create them; they need a SQL connection.
That second point is the most common misconception about deploying Synapse.
A SQL script artifact is a saved query TAB in Studio - deploying it does not
execute anything. src/synapse/serverless/*.sql is therefore deployed by
scripts/Deploy-ServerlessSql.ps1 over TDS, as a separate step in
.github/workflows/synapse-cd.yml.
Option semantics mirror the ADF module - see src/adf/deployment/publish-options.json.
linkedService.*-WorkspaceDefault* keeps deleteNotInSource away from the linked
services Azure creates with the workspace and refuses to let anyone delete:
<workspace>-WorkspaceDefaultSqlServer and <workspace>-WorkspaceDefaultStorage.
They are never in src/synapse/workspace, so without this the publish reaches
them and dies on ResourceNotDeletable - 400, 'managed by the workspace'. The
names are workspace-prefixed, which is why this is a pattern and not two names.
The integrationRuntime.* exclusion is load-bearing in one non-obvious way:
../workspace/integrationRuntime/AutoResolveIntegrationRuntime.json exists so that
the connectVia reference in LS_ADLS_Lake RESOLVES - the module resolves references
against the source folder, not the live workspace - and this exclusion is what keeps
that placeholder from ever being sent to Azure. Remove one and you break the other.
